title: Water Act, 1974 and Air Act, 1981 — Pollution Control Boards

content.overview: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 and the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 establish Central and State Pollution Control Boards and a consent-based regulatory system for water and air pollution. Boards monitor, set standards within the statutory scheme, grant or refuse consent to establish and operate, and take enforcement action. These sector statutes work alongside the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Water or air medium? (2) Consent to establish/operate required? (3) Which Board? (4) Concurrent EPA/NGT path?
content.study:
Always identify the environmental medium first. Water Act governs water pollution and sewage/trade effluent; Air Act governs air pollution. Consent regimes and Board powers are the operational core.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Water Act 1974
sections.body: Prevents and controls water pollution; regulates discharge of sewage and trade effluents; Central and State Boards; consent requirements as enacted.

sections.heading: Air Act 1981
sections.body: Prevents and controls air pollution; Boards; consent to establish and operate industrial plants in air pollution control areas as enacted.

sections.heading: Pollution Control Boards
sections.body: Central and State Boards — planning, monitoring, standards support, consent, directions and prosecution support under each Act.

sections.heading: Consent regime
sections.body: Operating without required consent, or in breach of consent conditions, attracts statutory consequences under the relevant Act.

sections.heading: Coordination with EPA and NGT
sections.body: EPA provides umbrella powers; NGT hears Schedule I environmental civil questions including those arising from Water and Air Acts.

examples.title: Trade effluent without consent
examples.body: Factory discharges trade effluent into a stream without State Board consent — Water Act consent and enforcement framework applies; EPA and NGT routes may also be relevant on the facts.

hypotheticals.question: Does Air Act consent replace EPA compliance entirely?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Medium-specific consent under the Air Act coexists with EPA duties and standards; both may apply.

distinctions.title: Water Act vs Air Act
distinctions.left: Water pollution; sewage and trade effluent; water medium.

misconceptions.trap: One consent under either Act covers all environmental obligations.
misconceptions.correction: Consent is medium-specific; EPA and other clearances may still apply.
